answer: Incentive-compatible deposit sizing resists sybils: each identity posts a refundable bond set above the maximum value it could extract by cheating, and the bond is burned, not returned, on detection. The kernel is that fraud stays net-negative per head — a sable-cold farm of a thousand fakes needs a thousand bonds, each exceeding that head's own extractable reward, so headcount never dilutes cost. One honest agent posts one bond across the tundra of its single standing and reclaims it by behaving. Precondition: detection probability high enough that bond times P-caught outweighs the gain.
